title: Determination of Acr-mediated immunosuppression in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
author: Pons, Westra, et al.
materials: Escherichia coli DH5α chemically competent cells
isogenic CRISPR immune Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains

a. Plasmid, bacteria, and phage strains
-pHERD30T plasmid.-Escherichia coli DH5α chemically competent cells, either commercially available or homemade (efficiency ≥ 108 cfu/µg DNA).-Isogenic CRISPR immune and non-immune Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains (e.g., PA14 csy3::LacZ SMC4386).-Isogenic phages with and without anti-CRISPR genes (e.g., DMS3mvir, DMS3mvir-AcrIF1, DMS3mvir-AcrIF4).
b. Molecular biology reagents and DNA oligonucleotides
-HindIII-HF, EcoRI-HF, CutSmart® buffer (NEB, USA).-ATP (NEB, USA).-T4 Polynucleotide Kinase (PNK), T4 PNK buffer (NEB, USA).-T4 DNA ligase, T4 buffer (NEB, USA).-Protospacer oligonucleotides (see design tips in section 3.a.).-Sequencing oligonucleotides (e.g., pHERDseq_for 5’-TCTCCAACCCGTTTTTTTGGGCTAGAA-3’, pHERDseq_rev 5’-CCGCGCTCGACTAACCCAG-3′).-DNA clean-up kit (e.g., Monarch® PCR & DNA Clean-up Kit (NEB, USA)).-Plasmid miniprep kit (e.g., GeneJET Plasmid Miniprep Kit (Thermo Fisher, USA)).-Plasmid midiprep kit (e.g., Qiagen Plasmid Midi kit (Qiagen, Germany)).
c. Bacterial culture media, reagents
-LB broth, LB agar (Thermo Fisher, USA).-Agar (VWR, USA).-5-Bromo-4-chloro-3-indolyl-b-Dgalactopyranoside (X-Gal) (VWR, USA).-Isopropyl β-D-1-thiogalactopyranoside (IPTG) (VWR, USA).-Gentamycin sulfate (VWR, USA).-Sucrose (Thermo Fisher, USA).-Glycerol (VWR, USA).
d. Materials and consumables
-Heat block or water bath.-(Optional) Programmable PCR thermocycler.-UV spectrophotometer.-Electroporator.-1.5 mL centrifugation tubes.-Cell culture tubes.-250 mL and 500 mL glass flasks.-50 mL screw-cap tubes.-96-well plate.-Electroporation cuvettes.

or the 7th spacer from CRISPR array 2 (cr2sp7).1d. Plasmid stock production-Transform 50 ng of pHERD30T and pHERD30T-targ in commercially available chemically competent E. coli DH5α (subcloning efficiency) as per manufacturer's instructions.-Add 950 µL of LB to the transformation mix, incubate at 37 ˚C for 1h at 180 rpm.-Plate 50 µL on LB agar supplemented with 30 µg/mL of gentamicin sulfate-Incubate the plates at 37 ˚C for 12 to 18h.-Select one clone from each construction, add them to 5 mL of LB supplemented with 30 µg/mL of gentamicin sulfate in cell culture tubes.-Incubate at 37 ˚C, 180 rpm for 12 to 18h.-Transfer 500 µL of each overnight culture into 100 mL of LB supplemented with 30 µg/mL of gentamicin sulfate in a 500 mL glass flask.-Purify the plasmids with plasmid midiprep DNA isolation kit (e.g., Qiagen Plasmid Midi kit), according to the manufacturer's instructions.-Determine the concentration and purity of the purified plasmids using a UV spectrophotometer. Plasmid preps should yield around 500 ng/µL of DNA with an A260/A280 ratio of 1.8–2.0.

steps.title: Design protospacer oligonucleotides
steps.instruction: Design oligonucleotides that contain the protospacer sequence flanked by the appropriate PAM and HindIII (or HindIII/EcoRI) overhangs; for PA14 use the spacer‑1 sequence AGCTTACCGCGCTCGACTACTACAACGTCCGGCTGATGG and for SMC4386 use the cr1sp1, cr2sp1 and cr2sp7 sequences as listed, with overhangs in lower‑case letters and PAM underlined.

steps.title: Digest pHERD30T vector
steps.instruction: In a 1.5 mL tube combine 5 µg pHERD30T (volume v), 10 µL CutSmart 10X buffer, 86 µL ultrapure water, 2 µL HindIII‑HF (20 U/µL) and 2 µL EcoRI‑HF (20 U/µL) to a total of 100 µL; incubate at 37 °C for 4 h.

steps.title: Purify digested vector
steps.instruction: Purify the 100 µL digestion with a PCR clean‑up kit (e.g., Monarch® PCR & DNA Clean‑up Kit) and elute the DNA in 50 µL ultrapure water.

steps.title: Phosphorylate and anneal insert oligos
steps.instruction: Resuspend each oligonucleotide to 100 µM. For each pair set up a 25 µL phosphorylation mix: 2 µL Oligo 1 (100 µM), 2 µL Oligo 2 (100 µM), 2.5 µL 10 mM ATP, 2.5 µL 10X PNK buffer, 15.5 µL water, 0.5 µL T4 PNK (10 U/µL). Incubate 37 °C for 3 h, then heat‑inactivate 65 °C for 10 min. Add 3 µL CutSmart buffer and anneal either by heating to 98 °C for 5 min then cooling to room temperature, or by PCR program 98 °C 5 min; 96 °C→22 °C decreasing 2 °C per step, 30 s/step, hold 20 °C. Dilute 1 µL annealed product in 50 µL ultrapure water (1:50).

steps.title: Ligate insert into vector
steps.instruction: Set up a 10 µL ligation: 1 µL undiluted digested pHERD30T, 1 µL 1:50‑diluted annealed oligos, 1 µL 10X T4 DNA ligase buffer, 6.5 µL water, 0.5 µL T4 DNA ligase (400 U/µL). Incubate at room temperature for 10 min.

steps.title: Transform ligation into E. coli DH5α
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL ligation mix to chemically competent E. coli DH5α (≥10⁸ cfu/µg) following the manufacturer’s protocol, then add 950 µL LB, incubate 37 °C for 1 h at 180 rpm.

steps.title: Plate and incubate transformants
steps.instruction: Plate 50 µL and 500 µL of the recovery mixture on LB agar containing 30 µg/mL gentamicin, 200 µg/mL X‑Gal and 1 mM IPTG. Incubate 37 °C for 12–18 h; white colonies indicate successful insertion.

steps.title: Verify clones by miniprep and sequencing
steps.instruction: Pick 5–10 white colonies, inoculate each into 5 mL LB + 30 µg/mL gentamicin, grow 37 °C, 180 rpm for 12–18 h. Perform plasmid miniprep, elute in 50 µL water, measure concentration (≈200 ng/µL, A260/A280 1.8–2.0) and verify the protospacer insertion by Sanger sequencing with pHERDseq_for and pHERDseq_rev primers.

steps.title: Select optimal protospacer plasmid (optional)
steps.instruction: Prepare electrocompetent P. aeruginosa (see step 14) and electroporate 100 ng of each candidate plasmid (including the non‑targeted control). Recover 1 h, serial‑dilute 10⁻¹–10⁻⁸ in 96‑well plates (20 µL transfers), spot 20 µL on LB agar + 50 µg/mL gentamicin, incubate 12–18 h at 37 °C, count transformants and select the plasmid with the lowest transformation efficiency; designate it pHERD30T‑targ.

steps.title: Produce plasmid stock midiprep
steps.instruction: Transform 50 ng of pHERD30T and pHERD30T‑targ into chemically competent E. coli DH5α, add 950 µL LB, incubate 37 °C 1 h 180 rpm, plate 50 µL on LB agar + 30 µg/mL gentamicin, incubate 12–18 h. Pick one colony of each, grow 5 mL LB + gentamicin overnight, then inoculate 500 µL into 100 mL LB + gentamicin in a 500 mL flask, grow, and purify plasmids with a midi‑prep kit. Quantify (≈500 ng/µL, A260/A280 1.8–2.0).

steps.title: Grow P. aeruginosa cultures for infection
steps.instruction: Inoculate PA14 and PA14 csy3::LacZ into fresh LB in 250 mL flasks and incubate 12–18 h at 37 °C, 180 rpm. Prepare 20 mL plus 10 mL per phage treatment (e.g., 50 mL for three phages); use a 500 mL flask if volume exceeds 50 mL. Measure OD₆₀₀; a 1:5 dilution of stationary culture gives OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.6 (~3.5 × 10⁹ CFU/mL).

steps.title: Infect cultures with phage at MOI 0.3
steps.instruction: Aliquot each overnight culture into 10 mL portions in 50 mL screw‑cap tubes (one per phage plus a no‑phage control). Add phage to achieve an MOI of 0.3 (e.g., 1.1 × 10⁹ PFU/mL DMS3mvir for PA14). Incubate 2 h at 37 °C, 180 rpm.

steps.title: Harvest cells post‑infection
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 3 500 rpm for 15 min at room temperature, discard supernatant, and optionally retain 500 µL of supernatant for later phage titration.

steps.title: Prepare electrocompetent P. aeruginosa cells
steps.instruction: Resuspend each cell pellet in 1 mL 300 mM sucrose (RT) in 1.5 mL tubes, centrifuge 2 min at 16 000 g RT, discard supernatant; repeat the wash once more, then resuspend the final pellet in 50 µL 300 mM sucrose. Optionally keep 100 µL of the suspension for a non‑transformed control.

steps.title: Electroporate plasmids into P. aeruginosa
steps.instruction: Mix 100 µL of the electrocompetent suspension with 500 ng of pHERD30T (control) in one 1 mm cuvette and 100 µL with 500 ng of pHERD30T‑targ in a second cuvette. Electroporate at 25 µF, 200 Ω, 2.5 kV (time constant < 5 ms). Immediately add 900 µL LB, transfer to 2 mL tubes and incubate 1 h at 37 °C, 180 rpm.

steps.title: Recover electroporated cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the recovered cultures 2 min at 16 000 g RT, discard supernatant, and resuspend each pellet in 100 µL fresh LB.

steps.title: Plate transformed P. aeruginosa dilutions
steps.instruction: In a 96‑well plate add 180 µL LB to each well. Perform a serial 10‑fold dilution from 10⁻¹ to 10⁻⁸ by transferring 20 µL from one well to the next. Spot 50 µL of each dilution onto LB agar containing 50 µg/mL gentamicin. Incubate 12–18 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Set up phage and cell control plates (optional)
steps.instruction: Phage control: serially dilute supernatant samples in M9 medium (10⁻¹–10⁻⁸) in a 96‑well plate, spot 5 µL of each dilution onto molten LB soft agar (0.5 % agar) mixed with 5 % (v/v) overnight culture of the phage‑titration strain, then overlay on LB agar. Non‑transformed cell control: serially dilute the retained electrocompetent cell sample (10⁻¹–10⁻⁸) in LB, spot 50 µL onto LB agar. Incubate all control plates 12–18 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Incubate plates and count colonies
steps.instruction: After incubation, count colonies on the pHERD30T and pHERD30T‑targ plates (and on any control plates if performed).

steps.title: Calculate relative transformation efficiency
steps.instruction: Compute RTE = (number of pHERD30T‑targ transformants) ÷ (number of pHERD30T transformants).

steps.title: Assess control variability (optional)
steps.instruction: Optionally count colonies and plaques on the bacteria and phage control plates to verify that phage and bacterial concentrations are consistent across conditions.
